title: Stein Kernelized Molecular Dynamics for Active Learning of Interatomic Potentials
claim: Our sampler explores diverse, informative regions faster than baselines during active learning, giving the fastest drop in model error.
layout: 3x4 contour grid plus two line plots below; rows compare methods across iterations
description: The top part has a reference potential energy contour map (a) and the initial NN potential at iteration 0 (b) on the left. To their right is a 3x4 grid of contour maps. Rows are Langevin (c), UDD (d) and a-SKMD (e). Columns are active-learning iterations 1, 2, 4 and 8. Red dots mark accumulated training data, cyan dots mark queried points, and dark blue traces mark sampling paths. Langevin stays trapped in the upper-left basin. UDD gradually reaches the lower-right basin. a-SKMD spreads across both basins quickly. The bottom has two log-scale line plots of test RMSE for energies (f) and forces (g) against training iteration. Purple a-SKMD drops fastest, with shaded percentile bands, against Langevin, UDD and SKMD. The eye goes first to the colorful contour grid, then to the purple curves.
caption: {Active learning of an NN potential, initialized at (b), using the M\"uller--Brown potential as the oracle (a). Contours of the NN potential at iterations $\tau \in\{ 1,2,4,8 \}$ of active learning by overdamped Langevin dynamics (c), UDD (d), and a-SKMD (e). The accumulated training data are shown in red, queried data at the current iteration in cyan, and path from the previous stopping time to the current stopping time in dark blue. a-SKMD leads to the fastest reduction in root mean squared error (RMSE) in the potential energy (f) and forces (g) of the NN potential, where 32 additional data are used in each AL iteration. Error is reported in terms of the median and 25th to 75th percentile range across 50 trials.}
abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) enable efficient and accurate atomistic simulations but depend critically on the quality and diversity of the training data. We introduce Stein kernelized molecular dynamics (SKMD), an enhanced sampling method that uses interacting particle dynamics to acquire informative training configurations for the fine-tuning of MLIPs. SKMD corresponds to a stochastic variant of Stein variational gradient descent that is adapted for molecular dynamics by incorporating asynchronous particle updates and a kernel of global atomic descriptors, which provides a symmetry-aware measure of configurational similarity. Unlike other enhanced samplers used in molecular dynamics, SKMD maintains the Boltzmann distribution as a stationary distribution of its dynamics in the appropriate asymptotic limit. This property enforces a balance between the exploration of diverse configurations and attraction toward high-probability regions of the energy landscape. We further propose an approach to efficient online data acquisition using an adaptive stopping criterion that selects non-redundant training data over the course of simulation. We demonstrate SKMD for the active learning of a neural network model of the MÃ¼ller--Brown potential, a MACE interatomic potential for alanine dipeptide, and a MACE foundation model with a DFT oracle for predicting the Pandey reconstruction of the Si(111) surface. Compared to active learning baselines, our method achieves higher model accuracy in fewer training iterations.
